title: Setting Up a Secure Network Office
module: Local Networks · Hardware & Maintenance · Security & Applications
paragraphs: David is a network administrator at a modern tech firm. His daily duties focus on Local Networks, Computer Safety, and managing Web Applications. Every morning, he verifies that all workstation hardware—including desktop computers, flat panel monitors, scanners, and projectors—is running smoothly. To prevent hardware failure, he regularly inspects network cables, power sockets, and server docking stations.

David ensures that all office staff use ergonomic keyboards and optical mice to maintain comfort during long working hours. When employees experience connection issues, he uses diagnostic tools to test wireless signals and replace faulty cables. David finds his job rewarding because building a fast, secure network environment helps the entire company work efficiently.

title: A Slow Computer
paragraphs: On Tuesday morning, Mr Lopez calls the help desk because his computer is very slow. The technician, Maria, asks for his name and his phone number. She asks him to restart the computer, but the problem continues. Then she opens a remote connection and finds a virus. She removes it with the antivirus and installs an important update. After twenty minutes, the computer is faster. Mr Lopez is happy and thanks her. Maria reminds him that he should never open emails from strangers and that he must back up his files every week.

title: Building a New PC
paragraphs: First, Tom shuts down the old computer and unplugs all the cables. Then he unscrews the side panel and slides it off. He lifts out the old motherboard and aligns the new one with the screw holes. Next, he inserts the processor and the memory modules until they snap into place. After that, he slides the power supply into its slot and screws it to the case. Finally, he double checks all the cables, closes the case and powers on the computer. The new PC is quieter and more powerful than the old one.

tf.why: "First, Tom shuts down the old computer..."

title: Computer Safety at Nova Office
paragraphs: At Nova Office, safety is very important. Every employee has a user account and a strong password. The company changes the passwords every three months. The IT manager, Laura, installs the updates every Friday and makes a backup every night. Employees must not open emails from unknown people, and they should not use USB drives from home. Last month, the antivirus stopped a dangerous phishing email. Laura says that a safe network is cheaper than a data loss.

title: The Network at ByteNet
paragraphs: Carlos is a network administrator at ByteNet. He is responsible for the local network of the company. He thinks Ethernet cables are more reliable than Wi-Fi, but Wi-Fi is the most convenient way to connect mobile devices. This week, a switch fails and twelve computers lose their connection. Carlos replaces the switch in thirty minutes. Later, he configures a new access point in the lobby, so visitors can use the Internet. He loves his job because it is rewarding and every day is different.

title: A Busy First Monday at Global Admin Solutions (Modelo A)
paragraphs: Welcome to Global Admin Solutions Ltd. Today is Monday, and it is 8:45 AM. Sarah Jenkins is starting her new job as a Financial Administrative in the Accounts Department. She graduated last June after completing several demanding modules, including Accounting and Taxation, Financial Management, and Office Automation and Information Processing.

When Sarah arrives at the Main Entrance, she goes straight to the Reception on the Ground Floor. The Receptionist, Mark, greets her warmly and checks her personal details. He asks for her full name, home address, and emergency phone number before giving her a security badge.

Mark explains the layout of the building so Sarah doesn't get lost: "Right now, we are in the lobby. To get to your workstation, walk down the Main Corridor and take the lift on your left up to the First Floor. Once you exit the stairs or lift, turn right into the Break Area. Walk straight ahead past the HR Department, and you will find the IT Office on your right, right next to the restrooms."

However, Sarah's first meeting is at 9:15 AM with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the Executive Assistant in the Boardroom on the Ground Floor. Mark tells her to go down the corridor, turn right, and enter the room opposite the Open-Plan Office. Sarah checks her watch: it is ten to nine. She has twenty-five minutes to grab a quick coffee in the Kitchenette before her meeting begins.

tf.why: She completed Accounting and Taxation, Financial Management, and Office Automation and Information Processing.

tf.why: Today is Monday and it is 8:45 AM (fifteen minutes before 9:00).

title: Organizing Suppliers and Logistics at EuroTrade Corp. (Modelo B)
paragraphs: David Miller works as a Logistics Administrative in the Purchasing Department at EuroTrade Corp. Before getting this permanent contract, he studied a vocational degree in Administration and Finance, where his favourite subjects were Logistics and Commercial Management, Business Simulation, and Integral Process of Business.

Every Wednesday morning, David meets external suppliers. Today, a vendor arrives at the Main Entrance at 10:20 AM. After parking his van in the Parking Lot, the visitor walks into the Lobby and speaks to Elena, the Receptionist. Elena politely asks for his full name, company name, and ID card number to register him in the system.

Next, Elena gives him clear directions to the Conference Room on the First Floor: "Walk straight along the Main Corridor on this floor and take the stairs on your left up to the First Floor. When you get upstairs, turn right and walk all the way down the Break Area. The Conference Room is at the far end of the corridor on your left, right above the Toilets."

When the supplier reaches the First Floor, he notices it is twenty-five past ten. He has five minutes before his 10:30 AM appointment with the Procurement Manager and the Vendor Management specialist. Later, at 12:00 PM, they will visit the Warehouse together to check new stock deliveries.

title: Customer Service and Tax Consulting at LexFiscal Partners (Modelo C)
paragraphs: Laura Gómez is responsible for customer service at LexFiscal Partners, an administrative and fiscal consultancy firm. She holds a Higher Technician diploma in Administration and Finance, having excelled in modules such as Accounting and Taxation, Human Resources and Corporate Social Responsibility, and English.

At 11:40 AM on Thursday, a client enters the Main Entrance looking for legal and tax advice. He walks up to the Front Desk, where Laura greets him professionally. Before calling the tax advisor, Laura asks the client for his full name, tax identification number, and email address so she can open his digital file.

After registering his details, Laura guides him to the meeting area: "Please walk down the Main Corridor and take the elevator on your left to the First Floor. Once you get off the elevator, turn right into the Lounge. Walk straight past the Archive Room, and enter the Meeting Room on your left, right between the Director's Office and the Conference Room."

The client thanks her and checks the clock on the wall: it is a quarter to twelve. His consultation with the Accountant and the Legal Advisor is scheduled for 12:15 PM, so he decides to wait comfortably in the Client Lounge while reviewing his tax documents.

title: Behind the Headset: Life on the IT Frontline (C1)
paragraphs: My workday begins the moment I put on my headset and log into the support queue, prepared for whatever digital chaos the morning brings. As an IT helpdesk technician, I act as the bridge between complex technology and everyday users, troubleshooting everything from minor software glitches to major network failures.

While routine queries like password resets are easily resolved, the real test lies in managing high-pressure situations. When a main server goes down, panic spreads quickly, and the phone lines are instantly overwhelmed. Handling these moments requires more than just technical knowledge; it demands great emotional resilience.

Undoubtedly, the most demanding aspect of the job is dealing with furious clients. When deadlines are tight and technology fails, frustration often turns into hostility. My role is to calm the situation down, listen actively, and translate complicated technical jargon into plain English. It is a fast-paced and demanding environment, yet the satisfaction of solving a user's crisis makes the daily routine genuinely worthwhile.
